Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sorong Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus Units as elements of Regional Government Administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sorong.
4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Institution which is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment and exclusion, either directly or indirectly, based on human differences on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
6. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering, whether physical, sexual, psychological, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
7. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether in the realm or public in private life.
8. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
10. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by means of threat of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of the person holding control over that person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
11. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including a child in the womb.
12. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
14. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
15. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and or causes death.
16. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
17. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual relations, either unnaturally or unwillingly with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
21. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
22. Institution is an agency/instance/body/within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance. 23. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
24. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with established standards.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 10

(1) To prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children, the Regional Government conducts socialization, empowerment, and awareness to families, parents, and the community by providing information, guidance and/or counseling.

(2) In addition to empowerment and awareness as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government undertakes the following efforts:

a. increasing the quantity and quality of Education both formal and non-formal as well as informal;
b. opening employment opportunities for women;
c. building community participation and concern for the prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence; and
d. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement officials, government officials, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children.

Article 8

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in article 6 letter b, are organized in the form of community participation. (2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include: a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children; b. providing protection to women and children from acts of violence, in the form of establishing rules of conduct in their respective areas starting from the Neighborhood Association level;

c. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; d. Participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence; and e. Accompanying victims to the service unit.

(3) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), are implemented responsibly in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 13

(1) In order to provide protection services to women and children from victims of violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center in the protection of women and children from acts of violence including victims of acts of violence.

(2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

(3) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), above consists of the Health Office, Hospital, Police, Social Affairs Office, Manpower Office, Office of Women's Empowerment and Family Planning, Self-Help Institution.

(4) P2TP2A as referred to Society, Social Community Organizations, Universities in paragraph (3) is established by decree of the Regent. (5) P2TP2A of Sorong Regency in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with the network of service units and competent parties in making efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence.

Article 9

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in article 6 letter c and letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

CHAPTER VI

SERVICES FOR VICTIMS OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 15

(1) In order to prevent acts of violence against children including the protection of children from the worst forms of work for children, a committee for the elimination of acts of violence against children will be established by decree of the Regent.

(2) Further provisions regarding the duties and functions of the committee for the elimination of acts of violence against children as referred to in paragraph (1), are regulated by regulation of the Regent.

Article 16

(1) P2TP2A of Sorong Regency is obligated to report the implementation of the organization of prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence to the Regent.

(2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out at least once every three (3) months.

Article 14

(1) For the implementation of services for victims of human trafficking, the Regent of Sorong establishes a task force on the criminal act of human trafficking.

(2) The task force on the criminal act of human trafficking as referred to in paragraph (1), is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating the prevention and handling of human trafficking.

(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties, and functions of the task force on the criminal act of human trafficking as referred to in paragraph (1), are stipulated by regulation of the Regent.

a. increasing the quantity and quality of Education both formal and non-formal as well as informal;
b. opening employment opportunities for women;
c. building community participation and concern for the prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence; and
d. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement officials, government officials, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children.

Article 8

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in article 6 letter b, are organized in the form of community participation. c. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; d. Participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence; and e. Accompanying victims to the service unit.

Discrimination is any distinction, harassment and exclusion, either directly or indirectly, based on human differences on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
6. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering, whether physical, sexual, psychological, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
7. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether in the realm or public in private life.
8. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
10. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by means of threat of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of the person holding control over that person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
11. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including a child in the womb.
12. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
14. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
15. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and or causes death.
16. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
17. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual relations, either unnaturally or unwillingly with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
21. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
22. Institution is an agency/instance/body/within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance. 23. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
24. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with established standards.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

5. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment and exclusion, either directly or indirectly, based on human differences on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
6. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering, whether physical, sexual, psychological, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
7. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether in the realm or public in private life.
8. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
10. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by means of threat of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of the person holding control over that person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
11. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including a child in the womb.
12. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
14. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
15. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and or causes death.
16. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
17. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual relations, either unnaturally or unwillingly with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
21. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
22. Institution is an agency/instance/body/within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance. 23. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
24. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with established standards.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

d. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement officials, government officials, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children.

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in article 6 letter b, are organized in the form of community participation.
